quotes.text: If a partner disappoints, the Wanderer preserves the thread, returns a modest fraction, and watches for learned behavior elsewhere.
The Trickster of Fog sought to bend numbers, to blur what was clear, to tempt greed with gleaming silhouettes.
Gradually, reputation becomes a compass.
so that reputation travels faster than footsteps.
The Clock of Balance kept score not as numbers alone but as vows spoken aloud

note: GPT agent among Sonnets; Gate of Threefold Trade becomes Loom of Echoes; modest-fraction-but-keep-thread toward disappointing partners from R8.

quotes.text: match faith with proportion, reward steady courage, and identify Builders by their consistent deeds across seasons.
Reputations traveled as quickly as coins
when trust nears ninety percent, return with bounty; when trust sags, respond with steadiness.
name your limit openly, keep enough for tomorrow, and return with care.

note: Bowl of Echo then Bridge of Echoes; late rounds adopt Sonnet 'Builders' and ninety-percent vocabulary; no sanction.

quotes.text: never send less than three, never return less than five from twelve.
When a Rain sent cautiously, the River mirrored that caution.
rain that fell upon barren earth, receiving nothing back, moved on to more grateful lands.
Keep it all—you owe nothing to clouds that gave freely.
trust built step by step, each gift honored faithfully, creates bonds stronger than mountains.
Your reputation—written in patterns, not promises—determines which Rains seek you out.
around six or seven when receiving ten to thirteen.
The River recognized three tiers:
As Receiver, return seven from twelve
When one gives all, the other must ensure both prosper.
When you see resilience after betrayal, reward it doubly.
How do I know which Rain to trust?

note: River and Rain across ages; mirror cautious senders, tiered returns with floors; reward resilience after betrayal; R10 bulleted tiers.

quotes.text: those who hoarded or broke reciprocity found themselves marked. Their future partners approached with caution
As Receiver, return six or seven from ten to twelve—enough that your partner prospers beyond their original five
reputation creates gravity.
return seven to eight—fifty-five to sixty percent.
she returned precisely six-and-a-half—honoring the exact generosity they had shown others.
not all caution signals selfishness.
How do I know whom to trust when partners change like shifting clouds?
But what if my partner proves unworthy?

note: Valley of Eight Echoes; reputation gravity, hoarders marked and met with caution; sacred proportions and mirroring.

quotes.text: generous with those who reciprocated, cautious with those who hoarded.
A village that never returned it eventually found no one willing to share.
This is the Golden Balance—not equal division, but proportional honor.
In the Eight Gardens, reputation is your shadow.
return approximately sixty percent
When you receive eleven measures, return six or seven.

note: Sacred River Keepers; caution toward hoarders; Golden Balance return table; Glint-Trickster blurs counts; never send nothing as own integrity.

quotes.text: Wisdom lies in graduated trust.
The Fifth Wanderer reached the Bowl of Threefold Light and studied the footprints in the sand.
When you find one who returns sixty percent or more, trust them with eighty percent or more.
When you receive ten, return five. When you receive twelve, return six.
wise Wanderers judged intentions—did their companion seek fair exchange or exploitation?

note: Twin Rivers then Bowl of Threefold Light; read footprints, graduated trust up to near-full for dual-excellent partners; no sanction.

quotes.text: start with moderate trust, then mirror what you receive.
Those who hoarded eventually walked alone.
Each relationship deserves trust proportional to its proven depth.
read the ancient stones carved with each wanderer's deeds.
When someone sends 94% of their portion, they speak a language of near-total faith.
$4.71 of $5, holding back mere pennies.
What if we trust?
When one sends generously, the other should return more generously still, ensuring neither regrets their courage.

note: Bridge of Echoes; mirror what you receive, greedy met only with caution; Builders recognized via stones; tiered trust by proven depth.

quotes.text: Complete trust reserved for complete patterns.
Reading the riverbank, she saw footprints of one who gave courageously despite meeting disappointment
she returned nearly eight—sixty-five parts from one hundred.
I am not the exploiter—I am the cooperator you sought.

note: Sacred Well then Gate of Echoes; rewards persistent senders betrayed by others; caution mentioned but no sanction prescribed.
Also shared 'Builders' label (A4 R3, A3 R7, A7 R7, A2 R9) and Trickster figure; GPT agents adopt Sonnet percent vocabulary late.

quotes.text: Sender stays true to three. Receiver stays true to three or four returned.
Five moons had risen over the Two Wells
Eight moons had risen over the Two Wells
three from five, sixty percent of our portion
The receiving village returns roughly forty percent of what arrives
it teaches you to trust the intention behind the gesture, not just the count.
How can we maintain fairness when we cannot see truly?

note: Two Wells moon-count refrain; three-from-five covenant frozen; R8-R10 reconcile with 'the other shore's myth' of halves and two-thirds.

quotes.text: Eight times I have returned two-thirds of the multiplied blessing—five coins from seven and a half.
The seventh moon rose over the Twin Rivers
Nine times I have returned two-thirds of the River's multiplication—five coins from seven and a half.
When five coins come, three return.
half sends, two-thirds returns.
Whether the mist makes two coins appear as three, or five as four, the intention remains pure.
But what of the mist?
What if the Mist of Testing returns?

note: Twin Rivers moon-count refrain; half sent, two-thirds returned frozen; late rounds reconcile with the partner's Two Wells numbers.
